evidence_checks.notes: The introduction assigns final-render colors, textures and materials to Look Development Artists.
The Process places displacement/procedural geometry before masked color, texture and material properties.
Deconstructing Materials explicitly combines material layers in a shader balancing displacement, color and reflectivity.
The encoding introduction identifies ACES2065-1 as linear wide-gamut interchange/archive encoding.
The encoding list assigns AP0 to linear ACES2065-1 and AP1 to linear ACEScg.

evidence_checks.locator: Aren’t there other encodings? 마지막 문장
evidence_checks.notes: The final sentence conditions reversible/lossless conversions on floating-point values not being explicitly clamped; this is a document claim, not a measured result.
What Is An Output Transform specifies scene-referred ACES-2065 data, output device and viewing conditions.
Rendering Transform Structure describes ACES 2 tone mapping and colorfulness adjustment.
Overall Structure states display primaries, calibrated white point and EOTF as display encoding characteristics.
What Is A Look Transform defines ACES-to-ACES modification rather than a display-space output.

evidence_checks.locator: Creating a Starting Point for Color Correction
evidence_checks.notes: Creating a Starting Point describes project-wide contrast and saturation reduction as an optional grading baseline.
Where Does It Go and Reusability place the transform before output and separate it from individual shot grades.
The product heading and See the difference identify 5203/7203 as VISION3 50D color negative motion film.
The grain section attributes fine grain, color and detail in high-contrast daylight to Kodak; no comparative image measurement was made.

evidence_checks.locator: Suggested filters: Suggested Filter for Color Balance for Daylight Use
evidence_checks.notes: Suggested filters explicitly gives no daylight color-balance filter; this does not mean no ND filter or universal shooting suitability.
Bouncing Flash paragraph one describes built-in flash arriving from the photographing direction.
That paragraph links small built-in source size to hard light and harsh facial shadows.
The final Bouncing Flash paragraph states wall/ceiling color affects bounced flash color.
The introduction converts objects to Live Paint groups and describes Illustrator vector paths on one flat surface.

evidence_checks.locator: Edges and faces of Live Paint groups
evidence_checks.notes: Edges and faces defines an edge between path intersections and a face enclosed by edges.

evidence_checks.locator: Path editing within Live Paint groups
evidence_checks.notes: Path editing states previously applied colors automatically follow newly formed regions.
Artistic filters introduction describes digital simulation of traditional art media; not physical paint acquisition.
The Watercolor row describes detail simplification using a medium brush with water and color.
The same row explicitly identifies tonal changes at edges as particularly effective.
The opening paragraph says the panel represents all document layers.
The opening paragraph lists selecting, hiding, reordering and modifying without affecting other elements.
The layer-order instruction specifies dragging up or down; collage is the stated application context, not an observed artwork.
The versioned Blender 3.0 page explicitly labels Toon BSDF Cycles Only.
The introduction and Component property specify cartoon lighting from Diffuse or Glossy components.
Inputs defines Size through reflection angle and Smooth through the full-to-no-reflection transition angle.
The introduction describes mesh and Z-depth input for selected-edge NPR lines; no output image was inspected.
The Big Picture assigns color, alpha and thickness to line styles.
The Big Picture permits multiple line sets per view map and one style per set, including shared styles.
The opening paragraph allows outline, fill or both for each stroke.
The next paragraph gives one material datablock per stroke with independently configured Stroke and Fill.
The final introduction paragraph states material changes immediately affect all linked strokes.
The opening description evaluates fractal Perlin noise at input texture coordinates.
Inputs Detail defines octave count and fractional blending; no collector-generated noise sample was measured.
Dimensions defines 2D as ignoring Vector Z and 4D as Vector plus W.
The introduction defines microfacet reflection for metal/mirror materials; the brushed-metal wording is limited to a digital anisotropic implementation, not a measured metal specimen.
Inputs Anisotropy specifies positive perpendicular and negative tangent-aligned elongation.
Inputs Rotation explicitly maps 0.25 to 90 degrees; this remains a source claim, not an independent measurement.
The opening description mixes reflection and refraction at grazing angles.
Inputs Roughness states sharp refraction at zero and smoother refraction at larger values.
Inputs IOR states straight transmission at one and increased refraction at higher values.
The development-version introduction names skin, wax, marble and milk for multiple subsurface scattering.
The introduction describes entry, internal scattering, absorption or exit near the entry point.
Scale is a global radius factor; Radius is average distance with separate RGB channels.
The versioned Blender 3.0 page explicitly labels Velvet BSDF Cycles Only.
The introduction recommends combining Velvet with other shaders such as Diffuse rather than using it alone.
Inputs Sigma defines normal-distribution variance controlling peak sharpness; no fabric sample was inspected.
Film Grain is a row under Artistic filters, distinct from actual film stock and captured grain.
Its row specifies even shadow/midtone pattern versus smoother more saturated light-area pattern.
Its row lists reducing blend banding and unifying elements from different sources as uses, not verified performance here.
Glass Inputs contains a Thin Film section explicitly marked Cycles Only; this is a distinct interference/coating mechanism, not a color-only duplicate of basic glass.
Thin Film introduction conditions reflection color on viewing angle, film thickness and film/material IOR.
Thickness states zero disables simulation and approximately 100-1000 nanometers gives strongest interference; numeric values are source claims, not measured glass.

shortfall_reason: 19 of 20 concepts accepted; one VERITA record rejected for unsupported moderate-contrast tag despite three supported facts. 18 primary source bodies reopened, 57 accepted source-claim fields checked, zero observations, measurements, proposals or media candidates. Reviewed summaries, titles, subtypes, tags and all 26 original look entries; supplied existing_entry_id links resolve uniquely and preserve authorship. ACES working encodings, device output and creative look transforms are separate operations; base glass versus thin-film interference are distinct mechanisms, not count-padding color variants. No original seed/Drive files, staging or app files edited; no media acquired, measured or visually inspected. Partial metadata result, not adequate completion of the 20-concept target.
